title: Stranger Things
synopsis: Hawkins. One more rift. The party is older, the stakes are bigger, and the math homework is, somehow, still due Monday.

nodes.text: The pool drains weirdly. The lifeguard, who is also Steve, notices first. Robin, beside him, is already calling Dustin.

choices.consequence: Strength in numbers.
Don't spook the town.

nodes.text: El is two states away at school. The call drops twice. The third time she just says, 'I'm coming.' She is.

choices.consequence: Trust the heavy hitter.
The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Don't wait.

nodes.text: The party reassembles around a kitchen table that has, somehow, more spreadsheets than the FBI.

choices.consequence: The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Discipline.
There is no taking “Move first” back. Adrenaline shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.

nodes.text: A transfer student named Vera knows more about the Upside Down than she should. She also runs cross-country.

choices.consequence: You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Allies.
You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Trust verifies.

nodes.text: Hopper has a cabin, a beer, and a tired face. He wants to help. He also wants you to be careful.

choices.consequence: You commit to “Ask for the gun.” The story records the instinct as “Older solutions” and carries it forward.
There is no taking “Ask for his old files” back. Newer solutions shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.

nodes.text: Max walks now. She is, against her own will, the quietest of the group. She has, you realize, opinions about the rift you have not yet asked for.

choices.consequence: You commit to “Make her tactical lead.” The story records the instinct as “Promote” and carries it forward.
There is no taking “Let her opt in” back. Respect shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.

nodes.text: Will starts feeling it again. He hates feeling it again. He does not, however, hide.

choices.consequence: You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Old talent.
You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Family first.

nodes.text: A 1960s newspaper has a rift story buried in the obituaries section. The pattern, you realize, is generational.

choices.consequence: There is no taking “Photograph the article” back. Document shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.
You commit to “Find the old witnesses.” The story records the instinct as “Sources” and carries it forward.

nodes.text: Vera admits she's been tracking the rifts since her family lost a brother in 1989. She is, you realize, also a survivor.

choices.consequence: “Make her co-lead” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Honor it.
The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Care first—follows you into whatever comes next.

nodes.text: There are tunnels. There are always tunnels. The town's pipes have been a map for years and nobody noticed.

choices.consequence: You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Cartography.
There is no taking “Go in tonight” back. Speed shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.

nodes.text: They bicker. They are best friends. They are working. The team is, in their own way, held together by them.

choices.consequence: The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Don't split.
The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Coverage.

nodes.text: A new monster — smaller, faster, somehow politer about doors. You hate that you noticed the politeness.

choices.consequence: The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Test it.
Don't give it time.

nodes.text: Hopper's old files contain the names of researchers still alive. One is, you discover, in Indianapolis. He will, on the phone, say one sentence and hang up.

choices.consequence: There is no taking “Drive to Indianapolis” back. Pursue shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.
There is no taking “Send Steve in your stead” back. Triangulate shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.

nodes.text: El, in the rain, in a denim jacket. The room exhales. You realize you have, despite the spreadsheets, been waiting for her exactly this long.

choices.consequence: Use the gift.
You commit to “Center the team, with her.” The story records the instinct as “Distributed” and carries it forward.

nodes.text: A skirmish at the pool. Nobody dies. Two get hurt. The monster retreats. You understand its pattern.

choices.consequence: There is no taking “Press the advantage” back. Move shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.
There is no taking “Plan the second” back. Discipline shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.

nodes.text: He says, in his apartment, 'You'll have to close it from inside.' He is, you can tell, telling you the truth he has been afraid to tell for thirty years.

choices.consequence: You commit to “Accept the cost.” The story records the instinct as “Brave” and carries it forward.
The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Hope—follows you into whatever comes next.

nodes.text: Max draws, on a napkin, a plan that involves all of you, no martyr. The plan is, you suspect, the one El has been quietly thinking too.

choices.consequence: You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Trust her.
You commit to “Refine it with the group.” The story records the instinct as “Together” and carries it forward.

nodes.text: The mall, again. It is, somehow, always the mall. The rift glows above the food court. You realize you have grown up in this building.

choices.consequence: The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Lead—follows you into whatever comes next.
You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Hold.

nodes.text: Vera offers to be the inside-person. So does Will. So, in his way, does Steve. You decide who.

choices.consequence: She's the runner.
He's the connection.

nodes.text: The rift, with the team's coordinated push, closes for the last time. The fluorescents flicker. The town does not, this time, lose a kid.

choices.text: Stand in the empty mall together
choices.consequence: There is no taking “Stand in the empty mall together” back. Be there shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.

choices.text: Walk out into the parking lot
choices.consequence: Step into the after.

nodes.text: Cars, summer, the team. You realize you will all, eventually, leave this town. Tonight, though, you are right where you should be.

choices.text: Throw a party at the Wheelers'
choices.consequence: You commit to “Throw a party at the Wheelers'.” The story records the instinct as “Joy” and carries it forward.

choices.text: Just go to Steve's job for ice cream
choices.consequence: The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Simple.
Some endings reveal themselves last.

nodes.text: You stay close — through college, through breakups, through one wedding and one funeral. The party never breaks up. You realize, late, that the rift was never the point. The friendships were.
You stay in Hawkins. You become a person who watches the town for next time. Next time, mercifully, does not come.

You leave Hawkins and never quite leave it. Wherever you go, a part of you is in that basement around that table. You take the lesson — that a small group of kids can save a town — into every other room of your life.
